title: Maple Leafs sign Gavin McKenna to 3-year, entry-level contract
content:
Gavin McKenna has signed his entry-level contract with the Toronto Maple Leafs.

The 18-year-old became the third No. 1 overall pick in Leafs history last month.

McKenna received the new maximum entry-level contract under the terms of the 2025 memorandum of understanding: He’ll earn a guaranteed $1,025,000, $1,075,000 and $1,125,000 in salary the next three seasons.

He’s also eligible to receive as much as $3.5 million each year in bonuses.

That includes up to $1 million for “Schedule A” individual bonuses, wherein a player earns $250,000 apiece for reaching thresholds such as 20 goals, 35 assists, 60 points and 0.73 points per game.

McKenna can earn an additional $2.5 million per season for winning a league-wide trophy or award or finishing among the top 10 forwards in goals, assists, points or points per game.

McKenna could bring serious value to the Leafs under the deal, including as a rookie and arguably the Calder Trophy favorite next season.

It’s almost a sure thing that McKenna plays with Auston Matthews at some point as a rookie, a connection that could prove immediately lethal thanks to the combination of McKenna’s passing with Matthews’ shooting. If he’s not playing with Matthews, McKenna might well end up next to another No. 1 pick in John Tavares and perhaps even William Nylander on the opposite wing.

Although it remains to be seen how McKenna will acquit himself physically as a teenager in the NHL, his impact on the power play figures to be immediate. He could play the set-up role on a revamped No. 1 unit in Toronto that includes Matthews, Tavares, Nylander and recent acquisition Darren Raddysh.
